title: deployment-triggered structured-output regression detector
creator: Marina Kirov
description: Build a deployment-triggered detection service that automatically runs lightweight, schema-aware regressions whenever a model version or serving configuration changes. The service should produce a numeric regression index and per-field explanations for structured outputs (JSON/typed responses) and integrate with rollouts and alerting so we can catch regressions caused by model changes, quantization profiles, prompt/formatting config, or tokenizer variants.
background: We frequently observe small model/config changes during rollouts that break downstream structured contracts in subtle ways (type shifts, missing keys, numeric scaling). Current evals are run manually or on periodic schedules and miss correlation to specific deploy diffs. This ticket implements a delta-triggered path that runs targeted validation against a representative sample set immediately after a deploy event.
motivation: Reduce time-to-detection for structured-output regressions tied to deploys, reduce noisy pager churn, and provide actionable remediation (rollback, field-level prompts, or config pinning). Improve confidence for canary rollouts by surfacing fine-grained schema regressions before wide rollout.
approach: Event source: listen to deployment/change events from rollout-engine with payload: model_id, model_version, config_hash, release_id, and canary_fraction.

Select sample set: deterministic sampling of 500 representative inputs per customer-cohort + synthetic fuzzed cases for boundary fields; prioritize inputs that exercise critical fields (based on field-criticality metadata).

Fast eval harness: run inference against both baseline (pinned) and candidate model/config with identical prompts and timeout budgets; collect JSON outputs and standardized metadata (latency, token usage).

Schema-aware scoring: compute per-field validation metrics: presence_rate_delta, type_mismatch_rate, enum_divergence_score, numeric-shift z-score, and structural-entropy change. Combine into weighted regression_index (0..100).

Explainability: for fields with large deltas, compute example-level attribution (show canonical samples where field transitions occurred) and suggest probable root cause (tokenizer/quantization/prompt-trim).

Alerting & gating: map regression_index + customer_criticality to severity and trigger console-alerts, canary-hold, or auto-rollback according to policy. Provide automatic noise suppression for <threshold regressions on low-criticality fields.
Telemetry & storage: persist per-deploy diffs to eval-metrics cluster with tags: model, config_hash, release_id, canary_fraction, cohort, and dataset_seed. Expose per-field heatmaps in console.
acceptance_criteria: On a deploy event, the detector runs within 120s and returns a regression_index for the candidate vs baseline.
Regression index calculations include presence_rate_delta, type_mismatch_rate, enum_divergence_score, and numeric-shift and are documented in the design doc.
Console displays per-field delta heatmap, top 10 example diffs, and a recommended action (observe, rollback, hold rollout, or manual review).
Integration tests: synthetic regression (intentional type flip / missing key) produces index >= 75 and generates a severity-2 alert in staging.
Ability to opt-in/out per-project and mark certain fields as 'non-blocking' via metadata.
tech_notes: Lightweight harness uses cached tokenized prompts to avoid tokenizer skew during comparison.
Baseline selection heuristics: prefer last stable release in same rollout lane; fallback to previous deployed model in region.
Weighting: default field-criticality comes from product annotations; allow override in project settings.
Performance: parallelize across GPU workers but cap per-deploy budget to avoid SLO blowups (configurable budget flag).
Storage schema: flatten per-field metrics into timeseries (no nested JSON) for efficient querying and alerting.
test_plan: Unit tests for each metric (presence, type, enum, numeric) and regression_index aggregation.
End-to-end staging test: simulate deploy event with candidate that drops 'price' field 80% of the time; expect alert and console visualization.
Load test: run 50 parallel deploy events and ensure average end-to-end latency stays < 3 minutes under staging resource limits.
Canary policy simulation: verify that canary-hold logic pauses rollout when regression_index exceeds threshold for critical customers.
risks: False positives from non-actionable formatting changes generating noise for PMs/SEs.
Cost: running targeted evals on every deploy may increase token/GPU usage; need budget throttles.
Edge cases: models that randomize output (sampling) increase variance — need determinism or multiple seeds.
mitigations: Use deterministic decode settings for comparison where possible, or average multiple seeds for sampled models.
Throttle evaluation budget by rollout lane and allow manual suppression per-release.
Expose per-field tuneable thresholds and an auto-snooze policy learned from historical signals.
